conviction_note: Most of the quarter is already public through Schwab's own monthly activity reports, and they point both ways: margin loans up, trading down. The one forward item is that the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16, three months before the December hike Schwab's July scenario assumed, and Schwab has said 25bp is worth $250-300m a year of net interest revenue. That gives a small positive lean (impact_sum +0.9). The scaled number is +0.21: abs 3.5 at p_up 53, because the 8.8-point put skew and this name's damped close-to-close reactions (median 0.78%) pull the sign toward 50.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $1.66-1.67 and revenue of about $7.19-7.22bn. Sources: AAII, 2026-10-13, next-quarter consensus $1.66 from 20 analysts, one upward revision and none down in the month (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517902-what-you-need-to-know-about-the-charles-schwab-corporations-q3-earnings); iTiger/Earnings Agent, 2026-10-09, $1.67 EPS and $7.19bn revenue (https://www.itiger.com/news/1112439436); Tickeron, $1.67 EPS and $7.21-7.22bn revenue (https://tickeron.com/blogs/charles-schwab-schw-q3-2026-earnings-key-metrics-and-what-could-move-the-stock-18602/). The sources agree within $0.01, so the bar is treated as sourced. Company guide from the 2026-07-21 call: FY26 revenue growth 17.5-18.5%, expense growth 9.5-10.5%, FY NIM about 3.00-3.10%, Q4 NIM 3.25-3.30%, one 25bp Fed hike assumed in December 2026, about 13% market appreciation (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/schwab-schw-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).
positioning_check: Short interest is 19.15m shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 1.1% of shares outstanding, 1.93 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/schw/short-interest, from the sweep row, read 2026-10-14). That is not crowded. The baseline shows 25-delta skew of +8.81 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI of 0.89. Front-expiry ATM IV is 58.5%, the event-implied move 3.94%, and the ATM spread 33% of mid. The stock is -8.77% over 20 days and -15.6% from its 52-week high: it fell 6.1% on 2026-09-22 on AI-disruption fears (Meta's Muse assistant, Altruist's planning tool), then Piper Sandler cut its target from $118 to $100 (2026-10-02) and Truist from $130 to $125. Sell-side remains broadly Buy, with an average target around $119-121.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), its first hike since 2023. Schwab's July 2026 guidance scenario (FY NIM 3.00-3.10%, Q4 NIM 3.25-3.30%) assumed a single hike in December 2026, and the CFO put the sensitivity at roughly $250-300m of annualized net interest revenue per 25bp. That is about 1% of the ~$28bn FY revenue run-rate per hike, and the 2026 timing gain is about $60m. The Fall Business Update at 8:30 ET on 2026-10-15 is the natural place for a raised Q4 NIM view and a 2027 framing that includes further hikes, since the Fed's projections favoured another 2026 increase.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-21): revenue growth guidance raised to 17.5-18.5% and operating leverage to 800bp, with the Q4 NIM guide unchanged. The stock closed +0.84% on the baseline window after trading down about 3% premarket on a BMO downgrade. Q1 2026: an NII miss ($3.14bn vs $3.18bn) sent the stock down about 5% intraday (Motley Fool, https://fool.com/investing/2026/04/16/why-charles-schwab-stock-is-down-today), but the baseline close-to-close was -0.37%. The NIR line moves this stock intraday more than at the close.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing a higher NIR path, rate-sensitive SCHW would have rallied after the hike. It fell instead: -6.1% on 09-22 and -8.8% over 20 days, with the selling blamed on AI and on fear of 2023-style cash sorting (TIKR, https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/charles-schwab-stock-fell-6-on-ai-fears-the-rate-hike-everyone-feared-actually-helps-it). Piper Sandler also cut its target to $100. The hike is public, though, and sell-side NII models will have moved for it, so this is the partly priced half of the guide.
findings.independence: The sensitivity figure and the December-hike assumption come from Schwab's own Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/schwab-schw-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), a different document from the Fed statement. The counterweight is cash sorting after the hike: September sweep balances are not yet published (see the sweep-cash finding).

findings.finding: Margin loan balances rose to $177.6bn at the end of August 2026 from $165.1bn at the end of June, +7.6% inside the quarter and +92% y/y. Interactive Brokers' September margin loans rose another 4% m/m to $105.2bn. Both support Q3 net interest revenue above Q2's $3.36bn as margin lending replaces lower-yielding assets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 NIR rose 19% y/y with bank lending +33%; the print beat revenue by 2.5% and closed +0.84%. Q1 2026's NII shortfall was sold intraday but closed -0.37%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. These are Schwab's own pre-released monthly numbers, and consensus revenue of $7.19bn (+1.7% q/q) presumably carries them. Only September's balances and the margin spread are new at the print.
findings.independence: The Interactive Brokers September 2026 metrics (margin loans +4% m/m, +36% y/y) come from a different company: https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/interactive-brokers-registers-6-y-y-increase-in-darts-in-sep-2026/. The June figure comes from the July monthly report (https://pulse2.com/schwab-client-assets-reach-13-04-trillion-as-july-core-net-new-assets-hit-record-58-1-billion/amp/).

findings.finding: Client daily average trades fell from 13.62m in June to 11.65m in July and 9.82m in August, and Interactive Brokers' September DARTs fell another 4% m/m. Q3 DATs are therefore likely about 10-10.5m against a Q2 average above 12m, and Q3 trading revenue is likely below Q2's $1.22bn, possibly by about $0.15-0.2bn. The CFO did flag summer moderation on the July call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 trading revenue rose 28% y/y in a quarter the stock closed +0.84%. No sourced case shows this stock moving on a trading-revenue surprise alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The monthly DATs are public and management guided to moderation, so consensus revenue growth of only +1.7% q/q is consistent with lower trading. September DATs are the only unseen piece.
findings.independence: The June and July DATs come from the July monthly report (pulse2, https://pulse2.com/schwab-client-assets-reach-13-04-trillion-as-july-core-net-new-assets-hit-record-58-1-billion/amp/), and the IBKR September DARTs (4.111m, -4% m/m) from fxnewsgroup. It shares the 2026-09-15 Schwab release with the margin finding, but it reads a different line from it.

findings.finding: Transactional sweep cash was $483.3bn at the end of August, +$6.5bn m/m after a $8.9bn July decline, roughly flat against about $485.7bn at the end of June and +19% y/y. The cheap funding base was stable through the quarter before the hike. September, the first month after the hike and the cash-sorting test, is unpublished and should come with the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2023, sweep-cash outflows after rate hikes drove a 24% NIR decline and large drawdowns. No sourced 2026 case of a reaction on the sweep line.
findings.why_not_priced: The fear is priced through the put skew and the post-hike selloff. Data through August says the funding base was stable, and the print delivers September. A clean September would remove part of what the skew is paying for; a drop would confirm it, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Interactive Brokers' client credit balances were about flat m/m in September at $186.2bn (fxnewsgroup, https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/interactive-brokers-registers-6-y-y-increase-in-darts-in-sep-2026/), so a peer showed no visible cash flight in the hike month. It shares the 2026-09-15 Schwab release with the two findings above.

findings.finding: The 20-day drawdown has a named, non-earnings cause: SCHW fell 6.11% to $100.35 on 2026-09-22 on AI-disruption fears (Meta's Muse assistant and an Altruist AI planning tool), then drifted to $95.94 with Piper Sandler cutting its target from $118 to $100 on 2026-10-02. Meanwhile August core NNA was a record $64.8bn (+46% y/y) and AAII shows no downward EPS revisions in the last month. The 8:30 ET Fall Business Update gives the CEO a platform on AI (developer productivity +15-20%, Schwab Assistant pilot).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A similar AI scare in February 2026 (Altruist's Hazel tool; SCHW -6.4% in a day) was followed by a rebound, with analysts calling it 'completely overblown' (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/ai-shockwave-schw-lpla-others-slide-disruption-fear). How the stock reacted at the following print to the narrative itself is not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: Estimates have not been cut (one upward revision, none down in the month per AAII 2026-10-13) while the price fell about 9%. The multiple, not the earnings, absorbed the drawdown, and record asset gathering at the print can answer it. Against that, the +8.8 put skew shows the option market expects more downside, and a narrative de-rating is not refuted by one quarter.
findings.independence: The Piper and Truist target cuts and the 2026-10-01 price come from ad-hoc-news/MarketBeat (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/zacks-cuts-charles-schwab-stock-to-hold-as-inflows-hit-record/70211272) and a WebSearch summary of the Defense World 2026-10-14 page. That page itself returned 403.

outside_window.finding: Further Fed hikes in the 2026 projections would add about $250-300m of annualized NIR each to 2027. This shows in reported results only from Q4 2026 onward; the window sees only management's framing of it, which is in the guidance finding.

rejected_candidates.candidate: JPMorgan Q3 2026 (released 2026-10-13): equities markets revenue +49% y/y, firmwide average deposits +2% q/q, AWM net inflows $263bn. Read as a strong-activity and stable-deposit backdrop for brokers.
rejected_candidates.detail: It is institutional prime/derivatives, not retail DATs. The deposit read is already carried by the sweep-cash finding through the IBKR credit balances, which are a closer peer.

rejected_candidates.candidate: The S&P 500 rose about 2.3% in Q3 2026 and about 12% YTD, in line with Schwab's ~13% full-year market assumption, so asset-management fees are on plan.
rejected_candidates.detail: This lands inside the company's own scenario, and August client assets of $13.41tn are already in the monthly report; it would size at 0 and duplicate the pre-released data.

rejected_candidates.candidate: AAII's consensus EPS of $1.55 for the quarter ending 9/30/2026.
rejected_candidates.detail: The same page reports it against a 7/21/2026 date and a $1.62 actual, so it is the Q2 bar. The same page gives the Q3 bar as $1.66 from 20 analysts, which matches iTiger's $1.67.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Zacks NIR estimate of $2.93bn (+31.8% y/y) for Q3.
rejected_candidates.detail: Q2 2026 NIR was already $3.36bn (iTiger 2026-10-09), so this is the 2025 preview served under the current year.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean runs against the +8.8-point put skew and the -8.8% run-up. The defence is that estimates were not cut while the multiple fell on an AI narrative, and that the Fed hike came earlier than guided. That defence is not strong enough to overrule the option market, so p_up sits at 53, not 55-58.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the stock's close-to-close reactions are damped (median 0.78%, Q1 2026 intraday -5% closed -0.37%), so the guidance finding shrank from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson 6 (inside what was guided or pre-released): margin and DATs are the company's own monthly numbers, so they moved toward 0, from +0.3/-0.3 to +0.2/-0.2.
Lesson 7 (sign against strong skew): the positioning/AI-drawdown finding shrank from +0.4 to +0.2 and p_up moved from 55 to 53.

Lesson 5: the drawdown is not unexplained (AI narrative, named target cuts), so the positioning finding was kept small rather than set to 0; macro-to-company (the Fed hike) was filed small with the company's own sensitivity as the bridge.
